The prior is Gaussian, making products and ratios of the Gaussian site factors closed form.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Expectation propagation is not guaranteed to converge and can oscillate or settle at different fixed points by damping and ordering; its moment matching is also a specific divergence choice, excellent for marginal accuracy and poor when the true posterior is multimodal, since one Gaussian must cover all modes at once.

layer2.mapping: Expectation propagation is the engine's recipe for folding hard, non-Gaussian evidence, like threshold events, discrete outcomes, and win-loss indicators, into a Gaussian belief state without abandoning closed-form updates: refit each evidence factor against the belief with that factor removed, match moments, and iterate. The cavity idea is the transferable core: judge each piece of evidence against everything except itself.
layer2.telemetry: Per-factor update logs for non-Gaussian evidence integration: cavity moments, refit site parameters, and iteration counts to convergence or damping.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core claim of this book is that optimization under uncertainty is a decision problem before it is a search problem, and this extraction follows that claim from its foundations to its failure modes. The foundation is Gaussian conditioning. When beliefs about an unknown function are jointly Gaussian with the observations, the posterior has a closed form: the mean moves by a covariance-weighted surprise, and the covariance contracts by an amount that does not depend on the values observed. That single update carries the entire book. Its practical face is that inference is linear algebra, executed through a Cholesky factorization whose cost grows cubically with the number of observations unless the covariance is compressed through inducing points. Its modeling face is that covariance design is where prior knowledge enters: stationary kernels, per-dimension length scales that learn which inputs matter, warping of the input space, and composition of simple covariances into structured ones.

On top of inference sits model choice. The marginal likelihood prices a model by the probability it assigned to the data before seeing it, which produces an automatic penalty for complexity, and the model posterior lets predictions average over plausible models instead of committing to one. Averaging matters because the alternative is not merely inelegant. The convergence theory shows that selecting hyperparameters by maximum likelihood can be catastrophic: the fitted model can assign the truth negligible prior mass in regions never sampled, and expected improvement then fails even on piecewise linear functions. A reasoning system that tunes itself on its own history therefore needs floors under its assumed variability and a model class that keeps expanding. That is a design rule earned by counterexample, not a taste.

The decision layer separates what is wanted from how to search. A utility function over final datasets defines value. Simple reward and global reward differ only in whether the terminal recommendation may be an unevaluated point, and that small difference carries real risk, because the global version can crown a point supported by almost no data. Information gain defines a different value entirely, entropy removed about a named target, and the book insists the target be named in advance, since information about anything else earns nothing. Given a utility, the optimal policy is defined by Bellman's recursion, one-step gain plus the expected optimal value of everything after, and the recursion's exponential cost in the horizon is precisely why the field lives on one-step lookahead: an acquisition function is the expected marginal gain of a single observation, maximized greedily, and every named policy is a particular answer to that one-step question.

Expected improvement has a Gaussian closed form that splits visibly into an exploitation term and an exploration term. Probability of improvement counts only exceedance of a target and turns risk averse once the mean clears it. The upper confidence bound prices optimism directly through a predictive quantile, and for Gaussian beliefs it is the same policy as probability of improvement under a target that drifts with the data. The knowledge gradient measures gain in the global reward and pays for that correctness with an intractable inner maximization. Thompson sampling replaces valuation with probability matching, choosing points as often as they might be optimal. The mutual information policies ask what an observation teaches about the optimum's location or its value, and their predictive forms become computable through Thompson samples, truncated normal approximations, and expectation propagation. Each policy also fails in a characteristic way: posterior mean maximization never explores at all and can repeat the incumbent forever, expected improvement needs a different construction under noise because the incumbent itself becomes uncertain, plug-in incumbents bias exploration, and the cheapest approximations are worst exactly in the high-noise regime where care matters most.

Computation gets its own veto power. Optimizing an acquisition function is itself a global optimization problem with vanishing gradients far from data, worst in high dimensions, so multistart search from space-filling designs is the practical standard, and imperfect optimization is sometimes even advantageous. Stopping is folded back into the decision framework: collect more data only while the best acquisition value exceeds its cost. The theory chapter then converts practice into accounting. Regret decomposes performance into per-step shortfalls against the optimum. Universally valid confidence intervals bound those shortfalls for the upper confidence bound policy, information capacity bounds how much any policy could possibly learn with smoothness setting the rate, and fill distance bounds worst-case uncertainty when observations are exact. Without a smoothness class the worst case is vacuous, since arbitrarily tall needles hide in the holes of any finite design, so every honest guarantee names its function class.

The extensions show the framework stretching instead of breaking. Unknown costs become a second inferred quantity with its own belief state. Constraints become probabilistic, feasibility becomes a probability multiplying improvement, and even infeasible observations earn their keep as information. Batches become single decisions over joint outcomes, which is where diversity comes from. Fidelities become correlated levels of one joint model under a cost-adjusted utility. Multiple objectives become a Pareto frontier with scalarizations whose blind spots are theorems, not surprises. Derivatives become extra observation channels in the same joint Gaussian. The through-line across all of it is that growth is handled by enlarging the state and the decision, never by bolting on an unexamined heuristic, and the book's own counterexamples are placed exactly where the enlargement is only approximate. A final thread worth naming is the book's honesty about provenance: its history chapter shows that nearly every policy it teaches was discovered, forgotten, and rediscovered at least once across five decades, which is itself an argument for recording reasoning in a durable form that survives its author, so the next generation inherits the operators and their failure regimes instead of reinventing both.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The genealogy of these primitives runs through several distinct lineages that the book deliberately braids. Gaussian conditioning descends from geostatistics and from Wiener and Kolmogorov filtering, reaching this text through Rasmussen and Williams, whose posterior formulas supply the computational core. The policy lineage begins with Kushner in 1962 and 1964, who first paired a Gaussian process model of an unknown objective with upper confidence bound and probability of improvement rules, and who already saw the optimal knowledge gradient style policy and dismissed it as virtually impossible to compute. Saltenis produced expected improvement in 1971, Mockus produced the knowledge gradient idea in 1972, and Jones, Schonlau, and Welch rediscovered expected improvement as the EGO algorithm in 1998, which is why the same operator carries several names. The information lineage runs from Shannon in 1948 through Lindley's 1956 expected information gain for experimental design, then to entropy search, predictive entropy search, and max-value entropy search. The regret lineage is younger: Srinivas and coauthors converted information capacity into Gaussian process upper confidence bound guarantees, and Bull and others then mapped where those guarantees fail once hyperparameters are estimated. The extension chapters graft on Kennedy and O'Hagan style multifidelity modeling, Pareto optimality from multiobjective optimization, and expectation propagation from Minka's approximate inference work.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The book is written for a reader who controls a real evaluation budget and is afraid of wasting it, and its rhetoric is organized around that reader's decisions. It assumes the reader can hold a probability distribution over an unknown function and will accept an approximation only when its error is named and located. Against the heuristic tinkerer, its recurring move is exposure: every folk rule is shown to be a utility function and a lookahead depth in disguise, so the reader is never allowed to believe a policy choice is innocent. Against the pure theorist, it places counterexamples immediately beside the methods they limit, teaching that a guarantee is a contract with conditions rather than a decoration. It also models its own author as a referee between camps, giving Bayesian average-case and worst-case RKHS analyses separate chapters of respect, and letting each veto the other's overclaims. The intended effect is a practitioner who chooses policies the way the book chooses words: by stating the objective, the assumptions, and the failure regime before acting.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The layers of the book veto each other in specific, checkable places, and the extraction preserves those vetoes rather than smoothing them over. The computation layer vetoes the decision layer's exactness: the knowledge gradient and the entropy search policies are normatively right and practically intractable in continuous domains, so quadrature, discretization, and expectation propagation approximations are admitted with their biases attached. The theory layer vetoes the modeling layer: hyperparameter estimation by maximum likelihood, the default practice, is shown to void convergence guarantees, so the theory imposes scale inflation and expanding model classes as conditions. The noise model vetoes the closed forms: expected improvement and probability of improvement in their textbook shapes answer the wrong question once observations are noisy, and the envelope construction replaces them. The decision layer vetoes pure information gain whenever learning does not change any terminal recommendation. The constraint layer vetoes unconstrained acquisition maxima by multiplying value with feasibility probability. No primitive in this artifact should be applied from a single layer without checking the vetoes recorded in its breakdown regime.

universal_lens: Read as a universal method, the book defines a complete grammar for acting under uncertainty when evaluations are expensive: maintain a probabilistic surrogate of the unknown quantity, state value as an explicit utility over final states rather than as a habit, price every probe by its expected marginal gain under that utility, and keep accounts in regret and information so that performance claims are auditable. Growth is handled by enlarging the state, adding cost beliefs, feasibility beliefs, fidelity levels, extra objectives, or derivative channels, while the decision rule's shape stays fixed. Approximations are permitted everywhere except in one place: the failure regime of each approximation must be stated next to it. Any field whose work is sequential measurement toward a recommendation, from laboratory science to forecasting, can be rewritten in this grammar without loss.
gsi_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Institute's research programs, the transferable machinery is experimental and inferential rather than predictive. Study design becomes Bayesian optimization over measurement choices: which biomechanical or tracking measurement to fund next is scored by expected marginal gain in a named utility, with knowledge gradient style valuation when the payoff is a better final conclusion. Competing analytical frameworks for the same phenomenon are held as a model posterior and averaged by evidence instead of being settled by preference. Information capacity bounds how much a planned data collection can teach given its noise level, which disciplines sample size promises. Expectation propagation integrates threshold and event outcomes into Gaussian belief states for longitudinal athlete studies. Multifidelity modeling joins simulation output, laboratory measurement, and field observation in one joint model with learned cross-fidelity correlation, and the stopping rule tells a study when additional collection no longer pays for itself.
gse_mapping: For the Galaxy Sports Edge reasoning engine, the book supplies the decision architecture around the forecasting core. Belief states over team and player strength are updated by Gaussian conditioning, so one result revises correlated beliefs jointly rather than as isolated edits, and automatic relevance determination learns which situational inputs deserve weight in similarity judgments. Weekly analysis effort is allocated as an acquisition problem: candidate lines of inquiry are scored by expected improvement in the final projection, by knowledge gradient when their value flows through other games, and by information gain about named targets such as an opponent's coverage tendency. The stopping rule ends work on a matchup when the best remaining inquiry no longer covers its cost. Calibration is enforced by the theory layer: confidence intervals must be universally valid for regret accounting to mean anything, hyperparameter estimates are floored so the engine cannot tune itself into blindness, and batch commissioning of analyses uses joint predictive value so redundant studies are not double counted. Model averaging over engine configurations, weighted by out-of-sample evidence, produces the published projections.
